frameworks.name: Hunt-Your-Own-Food Closer Model
frameworks.definition: Closers are responsible for their own outbound lead generation while also receiving inbound leads, keeping them sharp and ensuring they appreciate allocated leads.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that when a paid advertising channel (e.g., Meta ads) fails to produce results, the failure is attributable to the specific ads and conversion process used, not to the channel itself. The channel remains viable; the execution was flawed.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Any paid advertising channel
Advertiser concludes channel does not work
claims.mechanism: A channel's failure to convert is a function of ad creative quality and conversion process design, not inherent channel unsuitability.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that if a business can independently source high-traffic locations for placement machines, it should own those locations rather than giving placement rights to entrepreneur-franchisees, because the incremental value created by the entrepreneur (capital and local servicing labor) is the only justification for splitting revenue.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Franchisor or licensor can source locations independently
Entrepreneur-franchisee adds local servicing labor or capital
claims.mechanism: When the franchisor can replicate the franchisee's contribution, the revenue split destroys margin without adding capability.
bounded_by: Does not apply when servicing requires local presence that the franchisor cannot cost-effectively staff (e.g., single machine in a distant geography)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi estimates that a cold email outbound funnel for high-ticket physical product placement (robotic cotton candy machines at ~$15,000 per unit, 50% gross margin) converts at approximately 1 closed deal per 100 emails sent, yielding roughly $7,500 gross profit per 100 emails.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Cold B2B email outreach
Product price ~$15,000
Gross margin ~50%
Prospect is offered free revenue (placement deal) or a capital purchase
bounded_by: Based on one company's early outbound funnel; sample is small

claims.text: Alex Hormozi recommends scaling a working cold email funnel by a 50x multiplier (from 100 to 5,000 emails per day) as an immediate next action when close rates are high and the primary constraint is lead volume, not close rate.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Existing outbound email funnel is converting
Close rate on responses is high (near 100% in this case)
Sales team headcount is in place (4 closers)
Lead volume, not conversion, is the constraint
claims.mechanism: When unit economics are proven, the correct lever is volume multiplication, not process refinement; each 10x in email volume yields roughly proportional closed deal output.
bounded_by: Requires domain warm-up and multiple sending domains to avoid spam filters
5,000 (not 10,000) recommended as first step to allow process maturation

claims.text: Alex Hormozi states that at 5,000 emails per day with a 1-in-100 close rate, a 4-closer sales team each receives approximately 12-13 qualified leads per day (roughly 50 total per day divided by 4), converting to multiple closed deals daily from email alone.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: 5,000 cold emails per day
~1% response rate yielding ~50 leads/day
4 closers splitting leads round-robin

numbers.axis: leads per closer per day at 5,000 emails/day

bounded_by: Assumes domain deliverability is solved via domain warm-up
Assumes existing 1% response rate is stable at higher volume

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that having closers conduct 2 hours of outbound prospecting daily in addition to working inbound leads serves two functions: it keeps their prospecting skills sharp and causes them to value company-generated leads more than if they received only inbound.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Scaling sales team with both inbound lead allocation and closer-led outbound
Closers also receive company-generated leads
claims.mechanism: Closers who hunt their own leads develop appreciation for company-allocated leads; without the contrast of difficult outbound, inbound leads are treated as entitlements rather than earned opportunities.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi recommends distributing company-generated inbound leads to closers via round-robin first-come-first-served allocation rather than manager-assigned distribution, to maintain competitive urgency among the sales team.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multiple closers sharing a common inbound lead pool
Leads generated from email outbound automation
claims.mechanism: First-come-first-served creates internal competition that accelerates lead response time and prevents lead hoarding.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi states that for a business with a working outbound email funnel and high close rates, the correct immediate action is to automate email outbound at scale using domain warm-up, multiple sending domains (one per sales rep plus backups), and AI-driven personalization on the opening line, rather than hiring human setters to send emails manually.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business has proven email outbound converts
Goal is to scale from hundreds to thousands of emails per day
Sales reps are in place to close
claims.mechanism: Email automation sends from rep-named accounts at 10x+ volume without rep labor; AI personalization preserves response rates at scale by making mass email appear individualized.
bounded_by: Requires domain warm-up time before scaling to full volume
Backups needed because primary sending domains will eventually be flagged

claims.text: Alex Hormozi notes that AI-powered voice dialers have advanced to the point where prospects cannot distinguish them from human callers for the first five minutes of a call, making AI SDR dialing a viable alternative to human SDR teams for outbound prospecting.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: As of the recording date of this session
B2B cold outbound calling context
bounded_by: Quality varies by provider; assessment based on a single anecdote from a listener's experience

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that when a business's constraint is lead volume (not close rate), the diagnostic question is not how to improve conversion but how to increase volume by an order of magnitude (e.g., 100x: from 100 to 10,000 emails), and the scale-up should be driven by the founder rather than delegated to sales reps.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Proven funnel with high close rate on responses
Founder-stage business where scale has not been attempted
Email as primary acquisition channel
claims.mechanism: Identifying volume as the binding constraint redirects founder attention from optimization (which has diminishing returns on a working funnel) to multiplication (which has linear or superlinear returns).
bounded_by: Does not apply if conversion rate is the constraint
Does not apply if lead quality degrades at volume

examples.text: A robotic cotton candy machine business had four closers and one setter generating approximately 100 cold emails per day. Their response rate was 2-3% and close rate on responses was near 100%, yielding approximately 1 closed deal per 100 emails sent. Each machine sold for $15,000 at 50% gross margin, producing ~$7,500 per deal. Despite this economics profile, the founder had not scaled email volume. Hormozi's immediate prescription: scale from 100 to 5,000 emails per day via automation (domain warm-up, multiple sending domains named for each rep, AI personalization), distribute leads round-robin to existing closers, and have closers continue 2 hours of daily outbound to maintain prospecting skills and lead appreciation.

The cotton candy machine founder reported that Meta ads and LinkedIn did not work for his business. Hormozi immediately reframed this: the failure was in the specific ad creatives and conversion process deployed, not in the Meta or LinkedIn platforms themselves. He distinguished between a channel failing and an execution on a channel failing, arguing the conclusion should be to fix the execution, not abandon the channel.

practices.text: When scaling a cold email outbound operation, warm up all sending domains before ramping volume, use multiple domains (at least one per sales rep plus backups), and configure AI personalization on the opening line to maintain deliverability and response rates.

For a sales team receiving both inbound company-generated leads and doing self-generated outbound, distribute inbound leads as first-come-first-served round robin rather than assigning them to avoid creating dependency on allocated leads.

Before concluding that a paid acquisition channel does not work for your business, audit your specific ad creative and conversion process; do not abandon the channel based on a single failed campaign.
